text: You click 'buy' on a tiny widget, picturing it arriving neatly. You just want your item, simple and quick.
But when the package lands, it's huge! A vast box for a minuscule thing. You open it, puzzled by the empty space.
Is this for protection? Or just careless waste? Your mind conjures images of endless cardboard mountains and inefficient shipping.
The truth lies in the warehouse. Your item isn't custom-packaged, but dropped into the smallest *standard* box available on the line.
This standardization simplifies everything for the system: faster picking, easier stacking, less decision-making. The cost? A bit more material, a bit more air shipped.
So next time a colossal box arrives, you'll know it's not a mistake. It's the silent hum of logistics, optimizing for speed, not space.
